source_snapshot.title: fix(ingest): resolve JS and TS calls across parse batches
source_snapshot.body:
Fixes #374.

## Summary

Pre-scan JavaScript and TypeScript definitions into the repository-wide resolution index so streamed parse batches can resolve calls to imported symbols defined in later batches.

## Type
- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Test
- [ ] CI

## Changes
- Include JavaScript and TypeScript source files in the existing resolution pre-scan.
- Build their symbol index from parser-produced entities so it stays aligned with normal ingestion.
- Add a core regression test where the caller is parsed without the imported definition in its batch.
- Pin the CLI pre-scan extension set with coverage for all supported JavaScript and TypeScript extensions.

## Validation

- `cd ix-cli && npm test` (50 files, 649 tests, parser smoke passed)
- `npm run typecheck`
- `npm run build`
- `core-ingestion/src/__tests__/resolveEdges.test.ts` (33 tests passed)
- Anonymous 515-file end-to-end map: both the early-batch and same-batch callers resolve after the change; only the same-batch caller resolved before it
- The complete `core-ingestion` suite has six pre-existing failures identical on `origin/main`: two fixtures require the private `memory-layer` tree, one snapshot is stale, and three existing Rust/Scala expectations differ from current parser output

## Checklist
- [x] Tests pass
- [x] Smoke tests pass
- [x] No raw errors introduced
- [x] CLI output follows Ix format

## Release checklist (if merging to main)
- [ ] `ix-cli/package.json` version bumped
- [ ] After merge: tag pushed (`git tag vX.Y.Z && git push origin vX.Y.Z`)
- [ ] If backend changes: `ix-memory-layer` tagged and released first
- [ ] If `docker-compose.standalone.yml` changed: verified `curl | sh` install works

commits.message:
fix(ingest): resolve JS and TS calls across parse batches

Pre-scan JavaScript and TypeScript definitions into the repository-wide
resolution index so streamed parse batches resolve calls to imported symbols
defined in later batches.

The index derives these from real parse results rather than a regex, so they
cannot drift from what the in-batch path extracts. That costs one parse per
prescanned file, which was a synchronous main-thread loop — fine for R and SAS,
not for .ts, where it is most of a repository and an incremental map pays it for
every unchanged file too.

So the CLI now parses prescan sources on the worker pool it already runs for the
streaming loop and hands the results to buildGlobalResolutionIndex, which uses
them in place of parsing. Measured on this repo (180 JS/TS files), the index
build drops from 1.24s of blocked main thread to 1ms, with the parsing itself
moved onto the pool and spread across cores. Callers without a pool — tests,
library use — still parse in the index exactly as before.

Co-authored-by: KageBinary <ianjakobhock@gmail.com>

comments.body:
Rebased onto `main` — #380 and #384 landed since you opened this, so it was behind.

Authorship is preserved on your commit; only the base moved. Nothing else in the PR was touched, and the review comments above still stand as written.

Rebased onto `main` and pushed the fix for the blocking item, so this is unblocked from my side.

**Note the conflict**: #382 landed while this was open and touched the same three places — `INDEX_PRESCAN_EXTENSIONS`, the parser-derived block in `buildGlobalResolutionIndex`, and `resolveEdges.test.ts`. I merged both rather than picking a side: the prescan set is now `.go .php .r .sas` + the six JS/TS extensions, and both cross-batch tests are kept.

## The perf fix

Your design decision — derive the index from real parse results rather than a regex, so it cannot drift from what the in-batch path extracts — is right, and I did not want to trade it away. The problem was only *where* the parsing happened: a synchronous main-thread loop inside `buildGlobalResolutionIndex`.

`buildGlobalResolutionIndex` now takes an optional `preParsed` map, and the CLI parses prescan sources on **the worker pool it is already running** for the streaming loop, handing the results in. Absent an entry, each language block falls back to parsing in-index, so tests and library callers behave exactly as before.

Measured on this repo, 180 JS/TS files:

```
index WITHOUT preParsed (main-thread parse): 1.24 s
index WITH preParsed (pool did the work):    0.001 s
```

The parse work still happens — it moved to the pool and spreads across cores instead of blocking. Applied to PHP, R and SAS too, since all four blocks had the same shape.

Added a test that supplies a parse result whose entity does not appear in the source text: it can only resolve if `preParsed` is genuinely used rather than re-parsed.

## Verification

- `core-ingestion`: **35 passed** in `resolveEdges.test.ts`; full suite 280 passed with the same 6 pre-existing failures you documented, no new ones
- `ix-cli`: **698 passed** across 52 files, `npm run typecheck` clean, lint 0 errors / 38 pre-existing warnings

## Still open, and worth its own issue rather than this PR

An incremental map still parses every prescanned file, not just the changed ones — it is parallel now instead of serial, but a one-file edit in a 5,000-file TypeScript repo still does 5,000 parses. The real fix is caching the per-file index keyed on mtime so unchanged files are never re-parsed, which needs cache invalidation and is a bigger change than belongs here. I'd rather land this and file that separately than hold a correct fix behind an optimisation.

I amended your commit rather than stacking, since the fix is threaded through the same lines; you are still the author and I added myself as co-author. Shout if you would rather it were split.

reviews.body:
Thanks for contributing! The diagnosis here is correct and the index construction is careful — my one concern is the cost, which I think is larger than the 515-file validation repo could show.

## The part that's right

The JS/TS block mirrors the in-batch construction in `resolveEdges` exactly — same `kind === 'file' || kind === 'module'` filter, same `qualifiedKey(e)`, same name-keyed list of qkeys. That is the thing that usually drifts in this file (it is why the R and SAS blocks carry those "mirrors the qkMap construction at resolveEdges" comments), and you got it right, so cross-batch and in-batch resolution will agree on `dstQualifiedKey`. No correctness objection.

## The concern: this is the first prescan language where the prescan is the dominant cost

`buildGlobalResolutionIndex` calls `parseFile`, which is **synchronous tree-sitter on the main thread**. The streaming parse loop below it uses `ensureParsePool()` — a worker pool. So every JS/TS file now gets parsed twice: once serially in the prescan, once in parallel in the pool.

That trade was fine for the existing prescan set. Go uses a regex scan specifically to stay cheap, and R/SAS are niche and usually a small slice of a repo. JS/TS is the common case, and for a TypeScript repo it is ~all of the files.

Measured on this repo's own TS (176 files, 1.5 MB, `parseFile` via `core-ingestion/dist`):

```
SYNC prescan parse of all JS/TS: 1.02 s for 176 files  (~5.8 ms/file)
```

Extrapolating: ~5.8 s per 1,000 JS/TS files, ~29 s at 5,000 — single-threaded, before the parse pool starts.

**The incremental path is where this really bites.** In Path A:

```js
const remainingIndexFiles = filePaths.filter(fp => needsIndexPrescan(fp) && !changedSet.has(fp));
```

`filePaths` is the whole repo, so every *mtime-clean, unchanged* JS/TS file is read from disk and then synchronously parsed. Before this change `.ts` was not in `INDEX_PRESCAN_EXTENSIONS`, so `sources` and `remainingIndexFiles` were both empty and the cost was ~zero. After it, a one-file edit in a 5,000-file TS repo pays the full read + full serial parse on every `ix map`. That is the fast path this cache exists to protect.

At 515 files this is ~3 s and reads as acceptable, which I suspect is why it did not surface in your validation.

## Options, roughly in order of preference

1. **Run the prescan through the existing worker pool.** `ensureParsePool()` already exists in `ingest.ts` and is already parallel. It would need `buildGlobalResolutionIndex` to accept pre-parsed entities (or an async variant) rather than calling `parseFile` itself, since the pool lives in the CLI and this function is in `core-ingestion` — a bit of plumbing, but it removes both the double-parse and the serialization.
2. **Reuse the streaming loop's parse output.** The pool parses these files moments later anyway; only the ordering (index-before-batch) forces the duplicate.
3. **Narrow what gets prescanned.** Only files that are actually import targets of something in the changed set need to be in the index, which on an incremental map is a small fraction of the repo.
4. **Regex scan like Go.** Cheapest, but you deliberately avoided it for the drift reason above, and I think you were right to.

I do not think the fix has to be in this PR — but I would not want to land the JS/TS prescan without a plan for the incremental case, since that is the most common thing users do.

Happy to look again once you have picked a direction.

Blocking items resolved — see the comment above for what I pushed and why. Approving.

Verified after the changes: full `ix-cli` suite green, typecheck clean, lint 0 errors, and `core-ingestion` still at exactly the six pre-existing failures you documented on `origin/main`.
